# ninesixteen.video — full product reference

## One-line summary

ninesixteen.video is a native Windows screen recorder for true 9×16 portrait and 16×9 landscape capture. Frame with your cursor, zoom with Alt + scroll, record locally, and export MP4 with a one-time $49 Pro license.

## Who it is for

- TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts creators who want vertical clips without cropping
- Founders and indie hackers recording SaaS demos and build-in-public updates
- Tutorial and course creators who need tight UI framing
- Anyone who wants native aspect ratio screen recording on Windows without OBS scene setup

## Core features

1. **True 9×16 and 16×9 capture** — Pick portrait or landscape in Studio. Overlay, library player, and exports match your format. Zero letterboxing, zero crop step in post.
2. **Cursor-driven framing** — The viewport follows your mouse. Hold Alt + scroll to zoom from full desktop into a tight crop live while recording.
3. **Rule-of-thirds guides** — Compose shots intentionally mid-recording.
4. **System + microphone audio** — Blend desktop sound and voice with gain meters.
5. **Optional mouse click audio** — Mix click SFX into recordings (Studio toggle + volume).
6. **Encrypted local recordings** — Stored on your machine; nothing uploads until you export.
7. **Native Windows Graphics Capture** — Lightweight Tauri app, low CPU, not Electron.
8. **Virtual camera** — Device name "ninesixteen.video" in OBS, Zoom, Google Meet.
9. **Up to 1080p at 30 or 60 fps** — Defaults to 720p @ 30fps for lighter sessions.
10. **In-app library** — Preview takes, filmstrip thumbnails, slide-out player.

## Pricing

| Tier | Price | Includes |
|------|-------|----------|
| Free | $0 | Record, preview, all capture features |
| Pro | $49 USD one-time | Unlimited MP4 export to disk or Google Drive |

No subscription. No renewals.

## System requirements

- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit)
- WebView2 (installer bootstraps if needed)
- 8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended
- DirectX 11 GPU, 2 GB VRAM
- 1920×1080 display or higher
- ~500 MB disk for app; SSD recommended for recordings

## How it differs from OBS

OBS records full desktop or manual regions — you reframe for vertical social. ninesixteen records native 9×16 or 16×9 from frame one with cursor follow. OBS is better for live streaming and complex multi-source setups. ninesixteen is faster for short-form and native-aspect clips.

## Latest release — v1.1.0 (June 2026)

- 16×9 landscape recording in Studio
- Cinematic cursor overhaul (smoother follow, sharper cursor)
- Optional mouse click audio
- Faster Library (cached thumbnails, smoother scroll)
- Smarter viewport edge panning and Alt+F unfreeze easing
- 720p @ 30fps defaults
